targets.title: Thinking about God increases acceptance of artificial intelligence in decision-making
targets.evidence_quote: The importance of the research question, coupled with the underpowered studies, motivated us to replicate all online studies conducted by Karataş and Cutright (Studies 1, 2a, 2b, 3, and 5).
targets.outcome_quote: Fig. 1  omits a conceptual replication of Study 1 that produced a nonsignificant effect in the  opposite  direction of the original Study 1,  t (279) = −1.78,  P  = 0.077,  r  = −0.10 and a replication of Study 5 that successfully replicated the original result but whose experimental materials included a typographical error that presented inconsistent and potentially confusing information to participants in one experimental condition,  t (872) = 2.26,  P  = 0.024,  r  = 0.09.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The five principal replications found no significant effect; an additional conceptual replication had an opposite nonsignificant effect, while an additional Study 5 replication is explicitly described as successful despite a materials error. The final statement that evidence is less compelling is not an unambiguous overall failed verdict overriding these explicitly different comparisons.

reasoning: New larger samples directly re-test five experiments from one published article; additional attempts are aggregated with the principal attempts.
